title: Multiply three numbers: a three-factor equation chain on the passed `equation` template, with the easy pair bracketed (multiplication:multiply_three_numbers, NEW)

template.also: A COPY on the passed `equation` template (horizontal number sentences, the unknown in any position, TY-25 / DN-22; passed with division:div_facts' Standard and Fraction forms, redesign-passed.js OPS_DF, and with the fact family on the same equation frame). WHY equation and not `fact`: `fact` is the vertical two-operand stack (VA-70, TY-22: one operand over the other under a sum rule); 'a × b × c' with a bracket choice is a horizontal sentence with brackets, which is the equation frame's grammar (WDS 6 'Equation frame': lines for numbers, boxes for a missing number inside an expression). WHAT THE COPY CHANGES (and only this): (1) the payload takes three factors `terms: [a, b, c]` and `group: 'left' | 'right' | null` (equationParts today builds a op b = c); brackets are printed glyphs at the working digit size, weight 400, in a 0.4 em track each (a new literal in equation(); TY-6 lists no bracket glyph - add one line); (2) a CHAIN layout of up to three lines with the '=' signs in one column: line 1 the problem '(2 × 5) × 7', line 2 '= [ ] × 7' (the inner product in a box: a WORKING place, ungraded, data-ws-graded=0 on paper, input.mq-wwork on screen), line 3 '= ____' (the ONE graded answer, a line right of '=', CL-6); with group null line 2 is '= [ ] × [ ]' (the pupil chooses the pair); (3) form 'both' prints two chains side by side (the two groupings), each with its own graded answer line; (4) form 'missing' is one line '3 × [ ] × 2 = 30' with the unknown a box (SL-3: every blank of that section a box). Generator: gen-operations.js (new multiply_three_numbers branch); provider js/modules/sheet/providers/ (operations: strings, workedSteps, wrongAnswer, footprint); screen-cell.js draws the same chain on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz. No new drawing, so no mock (the lead asked for a mock on the new drawing only).

summary: ONE new skill, multiplication:multiply_three_numbers 'Multiply Three Numbers' (WRM Y4.B4.S13; school grade 3; 3.OA.B.5 associative property). Each cell is a short equation chain: the three factors with the easy pair bracketed '(2 × 5) × 7', then '= [10] × 7' (the inner product, a working box), then '= ___' (the product, the one graded answer). The printed bracket is the hint that fades; the chain's three lines and the inner box are structural and stay. Later steps: the pupil picks the pair ('= [ ] × [ ]'), shows the two groupings give one product (two chains), and finds a missing factor. Products within 100 (the answer bounds the band, never the factors). Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing.
teaches: 3.OA.B.5 (apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply: 3 × 5 × 2 = 15 × 2 = 30 or 3 × 10 = 30, associative property). EE: none - 3.OA.B.5 has no Essential Element (data/standards/ee-math.json lists it under notApplicable; multiplication:mult_properties carries ee: [] for the same code). WRM: Y4.B4.S13 'Multiply three numbers' (verdict gap; build list mult_three; Y4.json missing: 'multiplying three 1-digit numbers, choosing the order (associative property: 2 × 5 × 7 = 10 × 7)'); improves Y4.B5.S2 (Y4.json: 'reusing mult_three: its associative regrouping (a × b × c) is the same move'). The proposal also lists Y4.B4.S12 'Divide a number by 1 and itself' - a numbering slip already flagged in Y4.json (Q3). standards-audit.js 3.OA.B.5 is partial with mult_three as its closing proposal.
research: Searched 2026-11-20 (WebSearch; no logins - a WebFetch cannot hold a session, so the MathWorksheets4Kids and IXL member pages were not opened; nothing was copied). MathWorksheets4Kids (primary): its properties-of-multiplication pages (associative: 'regroup and multiply', 'complete the equation' with a missing factor in the second grouping, 'true or false' groupings) - the search returned no MW4K page, so the content model is taken from its known public index and the sites below. IXL (secondary): grade 3 'Multiply three numbers', 'Properties of multiplication' and 'Solve using properties of multiplication' (public skill names: write the product, fill the missing factor in '(a × b) × c = a × (b × __)', choose the property). Super Teacher Worksheets 'Associative Property of Multiplication' (three numbers a problem, regroup them, answer key); Education.com associative-property sheets (the product is the same however the factors are grouped); Illustrative Mathematics task 'You can multiply three numbers in any order'; StudyPug grade 3 'multiplying with 3 numbers or more'; Fishtank grade 3 unit lesson 5; CPALMS / HCPSS 3.OA.5 notes (factors within the facts; three-factor products, students need not name the property). Sequence taken (not pacing): a pair that makes 10 bracketed -> the pair apart (5 × 7 × 2) -> any 1-digit pair bracketed -> choose the pair -> both groupings agree -> missing factor. Where our standards override: one chain a cell with a structural work line (sites print one bare line), 6-8 a page (sites 15-30), no property names to circle (P-21: the move is taught, not the label), black and white, Andika, brackets printed not coloured.
problemTypes: solve (default): '(2 × 5) × 7 = [ ] × 7 = ___' as a three-line chain, the easy pair bracketed (mtGroup printed); write the inner product (working) and the product (graded).

choose (mtBracket off): '2 × 5 × 7' then '= [ ] × [ ]' then '= ___': the pupil writes the inner product and the factor left over, so the chosen pair shows in the work (no ring-a-pair choice: the work is the production, SL-7).

both (mtForm 'both', the associative property shown): two chains side by side, '(2 × 3) × 4' and '2 × (3 × 4)', each with its inner box and its product; two graded answers; the key writes the same product twice.
missing (mtForm 'missing'): '3 × [ ] × 2 = 30' or '(4 × 2) × [ ] = 40' - one box, the unknown factor (2-9); products within the band.
equality true or false? (true-false / reason-it pages only, from the provider): '(3 × 5) × 2 = 3 × (5 × 2)' true; '(3 × 5) × 2 = 3 × 5 + 2' false.
progression: 1 a pair that makes 10 (2 × 5), side by side and bracketed: (2 × 5) × 7 -> 2 the pair makes 10 but sits apart (5 × 7 × 2): the chain gains a printed 'turn it round' line '= 5 × 2 × 7' before the bracket (Q6; the page never silently reorders the factors) -> 3 any 1-digit pair that is a known fact, bracketed where it stands (product <= 100) -> 4 bracket faded: the pupil picks the pair ('= [ ] × [ ]'), the scaffold change alone on step-3 numbers (P-1) -> 5 both groupings (two chains) -> 6 missing factor.
Number size (mtBand, one change at a time): products within 30 -> within 60 -> within 100; factors 1-9, never 0 (× 0 is mult_properties forms 3); 1 as a factor only on the 'within 30' band.

Structural (every item, every step): the chain's lines with '=' in one column, the inner-product box, the answer line. Hint (fades first): the printed bracket; on Guided the bracket is traced grey on the tries before it goes (INK-3).

drawing.sizes: Working digits 22 / 28 pt (M / L) on the horizontal-equation ladder (DN-11: L 28 / 24 / 22, M 22 / 20 / 18 / 16 by columns; content never shrinks below the ladder floor), 1 em slots for × and = (TY-25), brackets 0.4 em tracks; inner box B(3) x (Hw + 2) = 20 x 10 mm (M) / 25 x 12 mm (L) - sized for the widest inner product the band allows (SL-2: 100 at the 100 band needs 3 digits; 2 digits = 14 / 17 mm on the 30 and 60 bands); answer line B(3) = 20 / 25 mm (2 digits 14 / 17 on the lower bands), 0.75 pt; lines 1.15 x digit apart plus 2 mm (M chain about 3 x 8.9 + 4 = 31 mm tall, L about 3 x 11.3 + 4 = 38 mm). Widest line '(9 × 9) × 1' about 32 mm (M) / 41 mm (L); widest work line '= [ ] × [ ]' about 50 / 62 mm.
notes: Capacity (PROPOSED Q8, measured at build by ws-empty-band and the DN-22 fit; content never shrinks): solve / choose 2 across: M 8 (2 x 4) / L 6 (2 x 3); both (two chains a cell, full width): M 4 / L 3; missing (one line): M 10 (2 x 5) / L 8 (2 x 4). Independent default 6 is the WDS 12.1 ceiling for standard problems; DN-1a dense packing allows 20 / 12 at M / L, we stay well under.

Item guards: three factors 1-9 (no 0); the product within the band; the bracketed pair's product a known fact (<= 100) and, on steps 1-2, exactly 10; no two items with the same multiset of factors on a page; the factor order and the group position each a separate seeded draw (L10: 'left' / 'right' must vary, never alternate); the answer never equals a printed number; on 'both' the two inner products differ (else both chains are the same).

Answer slots (VQ-2): solve / choose - ONE graded answer (the product line); the inner box (and the left-over factor box on 'choose') are working places, marked as typed on screen, never scored; both - two graded answers (one per chain); missing - one graded box.
Key (AK-1, AK-2): the same chain with the inner product, the left-over factor and the product written in place, in key ink.
Screen twin: the same chain in --mq-k2 px; the boxes are typed inputs (48 px targets); '=' column kept; at 820 px the 'both' form stacks its two chains.

Instruction strings (contract.js library, NEW, <= 8 words, PROPOSED Q9): 'mult3' 'Multiply the pair in brackets first.'; 'mult3-choose' 'Pick an easy pair. Multiply it first.'; 'mult3-both' 'Multiply both ways. Write each product.'; 'mult3-missing' 'Write the missing factor.'. iCan: 'I can multiply three numbers.'

Say frame (the model's Say: band, oral): '2 times 5 is 10. 10 times 7 is 70.' / 'I multiply the easy pair first.' / both: 'Both ways make 24.' Lesson routine (PROPOSED, prereqs.js): 1 Find an easy pair (a 10, or a fact I know). 2 Multiply the pair. 3 Multiply by the last number. 4 Say it. Chant: 'Easy pair first, then the last one.'

Files the build touches: js/modules/gen-operations.js (the multiply_three_numbers branch); js/modules/sheet/cells/equation.js (the terms / group / chain payload, the bracket literal) and css/sheet-kit.css (ADDITIVE rules only); the operations provider under js/modules/sheet/providers/ (strings, workedSteps, wrongAnswer, footprint, misconceptions); js/modules/sheet/contract.js (the four strings); js/modules/screen-cell.js only if the chain twin needs a branch; js/modules/data.js (APPEND { v: 'multiply_three_numbers', l: 'Multiply Three Numbers' } to the END of SKILLS.multiplication, grade 3 in the grade map, SKILL_PRINT_SIZE 'standard'); js/modules/skill-options.js (mtBand, mtBracket, mtPair, mtForm); js/modules/skill-presets.js + data.js (the two presets, Q5); js/modules/standards.js (SKILL_STANDARDS 'multiplication:multiply_three_numbers': {ccss: ['3.OA.B.5'], ee: []}); js/modules/wrm.js (SKILL_WRM ['Y4.B4.S13', {step: 'Y4.B5.S2', partial: true}]; delete mult_three from WRM_PROPOSALS); data/curriculum/links/Y4.json (Y4.B4.S13 direct; its pre list kept (mult_properties forms 0, mult_facts band 100, arrays_groups, add_three, mult_zeros) ; the skill added to the pre of Y4.B5.S2 and of the cuboid / volume step that multiplies three dimensions, and to related of Y4.B4.S11 / S3 (mult_properties) and number_theory:factor_links_easy; the S12 slip fixed); js/modules/search-terms.js (CONCEPT_RULES 'three numbers' / 'associative' + SKILL_TERMS); js/modules/build-list.js / build-specs.js (delete mult_three; the visual entry vis_array_options keeps multiply_three_numbers as a host for the R33 array-of-arrays option); js/modules/standards-audit.js (3.OA.B.5 associative clause -> full when built; drop mult_three from its proposals); design/wrm-visuals/year-4.md R33 stays GAP (array of arrays is vis_array_options, not this card). Share codes: the new skill id and the two presets are APPENDED to SKILLS.multiplication and option keys appended to skill-option-keys.js; never inserted or spliced (four share-code systems index by position; ws-code-snapshot must show only a rising count).

options: Options (skill-options.js, keys APPENDED to skill-option-keys.js at build, PROPOSED): mtBand (O2 number size: products within 30 | 60 | 100, default 100 - the band bounds the PRODUCT); mtPair (complexity: 'ten' a pair makes 10 | 'any' a known fact, default ten); mtBracket (O3 fading support: true printed bracket | false the pupil picks the pair, default true); mtForm (task: 'solve' default | 'both' | 'missing'); O6 appearance: none offered - one chain look (a reason: the chain IS the representation; the array-of-arrays picture is vis_array_options, R33).

The 2026-10-17 check, option by option (Q5): mtForm 'both' is a distinct task (show two groupings give one product: the associative property itself, IXL's 'properties of multiplication') -> ALSO a preset skill 'Multiply Three Numbers Two Ways (Associative Property)' {mtForm: both}; mtForm 'missing' is a distinct task kind (an unknown factor) -> ALSO a preset 'Missing Factor with Three Numbers' {mtForm: missing}; mtBracket false is a scaffold fade -> plain; mtPair and mtBand are number-size / complexity controls -> plain.
addsDrawingValues (PROPOSED): mtForm=both adds a second chain (a page holds 4 / 3).

Search terms (search-terms.js, same change; ws-search-terms gate): host - 'multiply three numbers', 'three factors', 'associative property', 'grouping factors', 'brackets multiply', 'easy pair first', 'times three numbers'; presets - 'associative property two ways', 'regroup factors', 'same product', 'missing factor three numbers', 'unknown factor'. CONCEPT_RULES: 'associative' and 'three numbers' + multiply -> the three.

openQuestions.q: Accept every role, host and option decision marked PROPOSED in section 7a?
Which passed template does it copy?
openQuestions.recommended: `equation` (horizontal sentences, passed with div_facts' Standard / Fraction forms): the copy adds three factors with a bracket group, the three-line '=' chain with a working inner box, the two-chain 'both' form and the missing-factor box (template.also). Not `fact` (a two-operand vertical stack). The first chain build is a copy on a passed template, so Opus low builds it, with the narrow copy-light critic (plan item 2) - unless the lead rules the chain layout a new drawing (then medium and a full critic).

openQuestions.q: The proposal lists Y4.B4.S12 (Divide by 1 and itself) as well as S13. Tag it?
openQuestions.recommended: No: a numbering slip (already flagged in Y4.json); SKILL_WRM is Y4.B4.S13, plus Y4.B5.S2 partial (the 'improves' step); drop S12 from the proposal record.

openQuestions.q: Which options are ALSO findable preset skills (10-17 rule)?
openQuestions.recommended: Two presets: mtForm 'both' -> multiplication:mult_three_two_ways 'Multiply Three Numbers Two Ways (Associative Property)' and mtForm 'missing' -> multiplication:mult_three_missing_factor 'Missing Factor with Three Numbers'; both grade 3, 3.OA.B.5, WRM Y4.B4.S13 (part). mtBracket, mtPair and mtBand stay plain.

openQuestions.q: A pair that makes 10 but sits apart (5 × 7 × 2): reorder the factors on the page, or add a 'turn it round' line?
openQuestions.recommended: Add the line: the chain starts '5 × 7 × 2', then '= 5 × 2 × 7' (printed on steps 1-2, the commutative move shown), then the bracketed line; the page never silently reorders the factors. From step 3 the pair is always bracketed where it stands.
30 / 60 / 100, default 100 (the G3 fact range); the band caps the product; 1 as a factor only on the 30 band; 0 never.
